frames.narration: Worker A asks for the lock 'invoice-7'. The leader commits the grant to a majority and returns a lease of 10 seconds with fencing token 33. Worker B asks a moment later and joins the queue behind A.
Worker A reads the invoice at 0.5 s, sending its token. The resource records 33 as the highest token seen and returns the value 100.

At 1 s Worker A freezes in a 15-second garbage collection. Its renewal thread is frozen too, so the lease is never extended and runs out at 10 s. The lock servers free the lock and wake only the first waiter.
Worker B gets the lock at 10.5 s with token 34. It reads the invoice, still 100, and the resource raises its highest seen token to 34. B writes 101 at 12 s and releases the lock.

Worker A wakes at 16 s, finishes its computation and at 19.5 s sends its write of 101 with token 33. It does not know the lease ended 9.5 seconds ago, and no check on the worker's side could have told it.

The token check sees 33 is lower than the highest token 34 and rejects the write. Without the check, A's write would have replaced B's with the same 101, and one of the two increments would be lost without any error.
Worker A learns that it lost the lock and joins the queue again. At 20 s it is granted token 35, reads 101 and writes 102 at 21.5 s. Both increments are in the final value, which is 102.
